title: the machine runs the tests and the reviewer judges: fail-first becomes a CI job on every pull request, a review reads CI's results instead of re-running suites inside its sandbox, and no round can take the board's port
acceptance: Why. On 2026-09-29 reviews took 17 minutes to over two hours (T-121 r9's review ran past 1h50m), most of it inside the round's sandbox re-running suites that start rounds of their own: macOS sandbox-exec cannot be applied inside a sandbox ('sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted'), so those suites fail or wait out timeouts, and the reviewer sorts environmental noise from real failures while GitHub's runner, which has no outer sandbox, runs the same suites correctly in minutes. Round 1 and 2 of this task tried to let a round nest inside a round; the reviewer found that it widened trust (any sandbox plus an environment variable skipped a round's own profile) and loosened the sandbox (unix sockets, listing the operator's home). The captain chose on 2026-09-29, from first principles: the reviewer's value is judgment; running tests - including fail-first - is deterministic work for the machine. Its own spec file, design/tasks/T-153.json, is committed on this branch.

Revert the nesting work of rounds 1-2: no nesting mark, no unix-socket allowance, no ancestor-directory listing, no nested-proxy chaining. The round's sandbox stays exactly as strict as on main except for the board-port rule below.

Fail-first in CI. bin/fm-failfirst.sh, run by a new `fail-first` job in .github/workflows/ci.yml on every pull request and part of the required `ci` aggregate: from the merge-base, it lists the test suites the change adds or modifies and the non-test files it changes; it restores the base version of every changed non-test file (and removes files the change adds), keeps the head's tests, runs each changed suite, and records per suite the assertions that went red on base. The job fails when the change modifies behaviour (a non-test file under bin/, board/ or adapters) and no changed assertion goes red on base; a change with no test changes, or only docs/skills, is reported as not applicable with the reason. Its report (per suite: red assertions by name, green ones marked 'guard') is the job summary and an artifact. Tested with fixture repositories: a change whose new test goes red on base passes; one whose test stays green fails naming it; a docs-only change is not applicable.

Review reads CI. bin/fm-review.sh starts the reviewer only once the head's required checks have finished (or after a bounded wait, saying which are still running), and puts into the prompt: each CI job's result, the failing assertions with their log lines, and the fail-first report. skills/reviewer/SKILL.md: the reviewer judges the diff against the spec with that evidence; it does not run suites that start rounds, a board or a browser, and never runs the full check; it may run small commands that need no second sandbox (reading, grepping, a single script invocation) to check a claim, and says so under Executed. Fail-first by hand is no longer the reviewer's step; the reviewer reads the report and challenges a test that is only green-guarded.

The board's port. darwin()'s profile denies network-bind and network-inbound on the board port (FM_PORT or 4173) and on every port listening when the round started, emitted unconditionally (also when the listeners could not be read); the pre-round bind probe runs on darwin only - on Linux the round's network namespace makes a bind its own. FM_PORT set but empty is an error (exit 64) in board/server.ts, and the board suite's helpers refuse an empty port. Tests for each.

Measured: the PR body reports the review-round durations of this task's own rounds after the change against the 17-41 minute baseline (and T-121 r9's two hours), and the fail-first job's CI time. Evidence: the required GitHub check and the gates, checked by firstmate at the merge gate. Workers do not run the suites themselves.
